page: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose server type powered by 4th generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors on the AWS Nitro system. The instance provides 192 physical cores running 192 vCPUs at up to 3.7 GHz on an x86_64 architecture without simultaneous multithreading, dedicating one physical core per virtual CPU. It is equipped with 768 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 5000 MHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per core. The instance includes 50 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth, features hardware instructions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, and contains no local instance storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark testing highlights exceptional parallel compute and throughput metrics across workloads. The server achieves top-decile ratings in multi-core evaluation suites, including a stress-ng score of 589,058.62, a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,751, and a PassMark CPU score of 143,375.95. Memory bandwidth reaches 651.82 GB/s on large uncached reads and 314.4 GB/s on large writes, driving top-tier in-memory performance such as 331.86 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 107.26 GB/s in static web serving throughput. CPU-based LLM prompt processing achieves top-tier rates across model sizes, though autoregressive token generation remains limited compared to accelerated alternatives.

From an operational perspective, the instance aggregates high compute density and DDR5 bandwidth within a single unified host, minimizing cluster orchestration complexity for massive monolithic tasks. Because local storage is absent, persistent storage requires external network-attached volumes, making overall I/O performance dependent on storage attachments and network utilization. The platform is suited for memory-intensive in-memory databases, large-scale software compilation, distributed ETL pipelines, high-throughput caching, and heavy scientific simulation.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors at 3.7 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system delivers 768 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory in a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside 50 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth, while excluding local storage and GPU hardware. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top decile across Geekbench, PassMark, and stress-ng benchmarks, backed by memory read bandwidth reaching 651.82 GB/s. The instance excels in high-throughput data operations, generating over 331 million Redis SET operations per second and 107 GB/s in static web serving. While sequential CPU token generation poses inherent throughput constraints, m7a.48xlarge is well matched for large distributed caching layers, enterprise in-memory databases, high-thread batch processing, and large-scale software build workloads.
